MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The Ring camera feels like a useful next step because it works with my Alexa devices and connects to my earlier interest in home security without requiring a whole-home purchase.",
    "The rotating surge protector fits a practical need: my recent electronics purchases mean more devices to power, and rotating outlets would help accommodate their adapters."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "Another Echo display and the Fire TV Stick fit my interests, but I recently bought an Echo Show 5 and a Fire TV Stick 4K Max bundle, so these would duplicate functions I just added.",
    "The Echo Show 8 stand does not fit my Echo Show 5. Sharing the Echo name does not make it useful for the device I own.",
    "The thermostat and portable monitor suggest needs I have not expressed, while the basic wireless mouse offers no clear improvement over my previous Bluetooth and ergonomic choices."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My Alexa purchases seem to have been taken as interest in almost any Alexa-compatible device, even when installation requirements or a larger commitment make it less suitable now.",
    "My repeated computer accessory purchases seem to suggest I always want more accessories, but I choose them for particular functions rather than simply because they belong with computers."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My recent purchases matter because they show which needs I have already addressed; a useful addition is more appealing now than another device serving the same purpose.",
    "The exact device matters for accessories: I recently bought both an Echo Show 5 and its matching stand, which does not imply a need for a Show 8 stand.",
    "On this visit I would start with one security camera and choose one power solution; interest in those needs does not mean I want a whole-home bundle or multiple surge protectors."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognize my interest in Alexa devices and practical electronics, but miss the difference between a useful next addition and something redundant, incompatible, or unnecessary right now."
}
